source: user-led reconciliation during the B=4 1800s sweep audit (3f4204bb); vLLM source read via scripts/vllm_src.sh (pinned 3dbe092e); git-history pre-kernel numbers
summary: Full reconciliation of why the B=4 deployment E5 TPS (6.67-7.5) looks ~3x below the historical B=1 native E5 (~18.3-18.9) and the pre-kernel B=4 references, plus the fix (per_request_decode_tps + aggregate_decode_tps added to deploy-speed). NONE of it is a regression or our instrumentation; it is the metric-definition + regime + a deflated TPS basis.

historical_native_E5_B1.note: native MTP-5 is the UNTOUCHED incumbent; should be stable. All B=1, decode_seconds/spec_drafts basis.

pre_kernel_B4_native_E5.note: FR10 'speed starting point', RAW synthetic decode probe (fixed prompts, pure decode, client-batch), pre-tree-kernel
pre_kernel_B4_native_E5.FR10_VERBATIM_FLAG: 'metrics_sum_decode_tps divides generation tokens by vllm:request_decode_time_seconds_sum, which SUMS concurrent per-request decode seconds at B4 and is therefore CONCURRENCY-DEFLATED. Do not compare that ~8 TPS to E5. Use per-request median/mean.'

root_cause_chain: decode_time = last_token_ts - first_token_ts (output_processor.py:726, pinned image) = a WALL-SPAN, not a sum of pure forward times.
At B=1 (one agent) the span ~= pure forward time -> s/fwd 0.22, B-invariant (clean-regime native E5 B=4 0.21641 = -0.42% vs B=1 0.2182 CONFIRMS B-invariance).

At B=4 deployment (4 co-resident codex agents, enable_chunked_prefill=True) the span STRETCHES ~2.7x because between a request's tokens the scheduler interleaves the other 3 agents' prefill+decode -> s/fwd 0.6263 (1800s: 0.5961). REAL per-request latency under co-residency, NOT a bug.
derived_tps = committed/s_fwd = gen_tokens/decode_seconds_sum = EXACTLY the FR10-flagged concurrency-summed basis (E5 B=4 6.67 [600s] / 7.5 [1800s] ~ the pre-kernel deflated 8.74, same basis).

drafts IS per-request (x B/step) - verified empirically (committed/step = co-res 3.37 x 4.17/draft = 14.05 = gen_tok/steps 14.07) - so s/fwd's batch factor cancels; the inflation is the wall-span interleave, not a /4 error.

reconciliation_verdict.pure_per_forward_speed: ~0.22 s/fwd = B-INVARIANT, the number that 'should match' B=1==B=4 (and does, clean regime). The B=4 deployment 0.6263 = 0.22 pure + ~0.40 co-resident interleave.
reconciliation_verdict.native_E5_not_a_regression: B=1 ~18.5 TPS (1 stream); B=4 per-request 6.53 (measured non-deflated) -> aggregate 15.66 measured. Same incumbent through co-residency.
reconciliation_verdict.metrics_do_NOT_affect_speed: deploy-speed is INSTRUMENT=OFF: FR10_METRICS=0 + VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0 pinned+asserted (BI=1 would slow GEMMs), diag hooks inert (chase=0). Pair-dumps are alienware-side, fire once at end-of-response, never touch GB10 decode_time. ONLY the regime (interleave) inflates B=4 s/fwd.
reconciliation_verdict.why_no_prior_aggregate_B4_TPS: aggregate/wall TPS was BANNED as a basis (assert_speed_basis blocks tps/wall/req_elapsed) after the FR10 '~8 TPS' artifact + 'stale 2.336x'; project standardized on s/fwd. Cost = lost the throughput-reporting number, now re-added as reporting-only.

fix_committed: 585b1f02 on fr13-speedfix: deploy-speed now emits per_request_decode_tps (count/sum of vLLM request_time_per_output_token = 1/avg per-request mean-TPOT = non-deflated per-stream rate) + aggregate_decode_tps (gen_tokens over earliest-pre->latest-post UNION window / union wall = total GPU throughput, reporting-only) + annotates derived_tps as the concurrency-summed basis. Additive, no serve restart (re-reduced E5 offline; applies forward to cat9+). E5 1800s: s/fwd 0.5961, accept 3.471, per_request_decode_tps 6.53, aggregate_decode_tps 15.66.
comparison_guidance: cat9-vs-E5 ratio on derived_tps is still valid (both concurrency-summed identically). For ABSOLUTE/cross-reference use per_request_decode_tps (per-stream) or aggregate_decode_tps (throughput). For pure KERNEL speed use the B=1 clean-regime s/fwd (cat9 1.030x native), NOT the interleave-laden B=4 deployment s/fwd.
